description.p: A native Nostr client with a GPU-rendered UI and a local-first event store: a follows-driven timeline, threads, reactions, zaps, reposts, and direct messages, all served from an LMDB cache on your disk and kept fresh by one live subscription.

Inline video plays through GStreamer, click to play, one player at a time, no autoplay: a tile's preview is a poster the publisher attached, a blurhash, or a first frame decoded locally, the video itself never downloads before you tap, and strict Tor keeps even the preview off. Keys stay in your secret store, relays are yours to pick (NIP-65), and private preferences sync end-to-end encrypted through NIP-78.

Editing your lists can no longer wipe them. Follow, mute, and bookmark lists were rebuilt from what the session had in memory when you toggled, so a change made in the first seconds after launch (before your lists finished loading), or one made from another client mid-session, could publish a shorter list over the relay's full one. Every list publish now starts from the newest copy of the list Satori knows (the local store, with one fallback fetch when it has none), keeps the parts of the old event a toggle does not touch (a follow list's relay hints, a mute list's public entries), and refuses to publish a removal when it has nothing to remove from. This is the same shape Amethyst ships, proven there by years of daily use.

Your relationships live on one page now. Your profile picture at the top of the rail opens the me menu, and its new Network row opens a page with two segments: Following (people you follow) and Muted (people you have silenced, which until now you could not see anywhere). Every row carries the actions that fit the relationship: follow or unfollow, mute or unmute, right there in the list, no more visiting each profile to manage who you hear from. An early build also tried a Followers segment: Nostr has no global followers list, the reverse lookup undersold the real number by an order of magnitude, and a confidently wrong list is worse than its absence, so it did not ship.

The event store keeps itself lean. The store's file only ever grows, even after notes are deleted or pruned: the space stays allocated until the store is rebuilt. Satori has shipped an explicit offline rebuild (the --vacuum flag) since 0.5.0; the app now runs the same verified rebuild automatically when the store has grown half again past its size at the last rebuild (at least 64 MiB of growth, so small stores never churn) — and the rebuild runs in the background while you use the app, never in front of it: the slimmed store swaps in at a later launch, so no launch waits on the rebuild.

Alpine packages are signed by a persistent key: one keypair signs every release, on both architectures, so the "UNTRUSTED signature" warning apk showed on first install is fixed for good. Trust the .pub once and every future version verifies clean; the release page carries the trust-and-install instructions.

Connections come back faster. A full audit of the relay connection lifecycle surfaced real gaps in how Satori recovers: the reconnect nudge after sleep was a no-op in exactly the case it existed for (every relay asleep-disconnected), so recovery rode the SDK's own timers, up to a minute or more. The nudge now force-retries each dead relay the moment the machine wakes, short lid-closes included; relays added for routed reads actually connect now (some followed-author reads could sit empty for a whole session); the live bell's re-arm no longer has terminal failure paths; the wire column and engagement counts survive a relay restarting under them; and a relay that answered brownout queries with nothing can earn its way back into the read rotation.

@mentions inside note bodies now show people's names everywhere, not just in the notes and articles timelines. A mention in a note is a raw npub token that the app turns into a name by looking the person up, but page fetches only ever looked up note authors, so the same note showed a name in the timeline and a bare npub in the notifications page or on a profile. Page fetches now include everyone a body mentions, and the notifications and profile views patch names in as they land. Fixing this also un-broke the notifications page's receipt names, whose updates were silently dropped.

Notification rows carry the copy-the-event-id seal that notes and articles already have: it sits on the timestamp and copies the note on screen (the boosted note for a repost; receipts that show no note get no seal).

The Library has left the sidebar, and then the Library itself left: your profile picture at the top of the rail now opens a small menu with View profile, Bookmarks, Drafts, and Lists, and each one is its own page with its own name and back button. The rail is one icon slimmer and your own things live in one obvious place.

Threads stop flashing their images: a thread pinned every picture it contained against memory pressure, and on photo-heavy threads that pin silently ran out partway down, so the pictures on screen blinked out and back while you scrolled. Threads now protect exactly what is on screen like every other page, and the reply list no longer re-animates itself when names and context land in the background.

The live notification subscriptions survive relay CLOSEDs: a relay answering CLOSED for the bell's subscription (subscription pressure, a relay restart, an auth flip) used to lose it for good, silently starving the bell dot and the new-notes pill for the rest of the session. The live loop now re-arms both subscriptions when a relay takes one away, and the routed relay trim evicts stale relays for real while re-stamping the relays still hosting subscriptions, so trimming can never kill the live bell.

Relays that refuse a query for a satisfiable reason are no longer treated as read-denials: purplepag.es (the profile and graph relay) rejected our wider queries with "limit too high: 1000 (max 500)", and each refusal marked the relay read-dead for 12 hours, cutting profile fetches off from it. Limit rejections and NIP-42 auth challenges now leave the relay in the read rotation, our own queries cap at 500 events (the strictest mainstream limit) so strict relays answer them, genuine refusals still mark the relay read-dead, and refusal logs now include the relay's reason text.

The routed fan-out no longer dials other people's personal firehose endpoints (filter.nostr.wine-style urls with a customer npub in the path): only that key can answer the auth challenge, so a follow's endpoint was an endless authenticate-and-fail loop. Our own endpoint, if listed, still works. A relay refusing our signed auth now logs as "auth rejected" instead of vanishing, and a mock auth-relay test proves the challenge-sign-accept dance delivers.

The notifications page now verifies that each row is actually about you: your key in a p tag, your key in an addressed a tag, or a reference to one of your recent notes. A relay that mis-served the mention filter could previously paint strangers' notes as "mentioned you". Zaps, reactions, and reposts clear the check naturally.

Video tiles earned their picture: a note's video previews its first frame instead of a bare box, big files and moov-at-end mp4s ride a guarded range-proxy, and GIF-encoded-as-mp4 clips play inline. Every note timestamp gained a copy button that puts a nostr: URI on the clipboard.

Notes with a plain link show a preview card: the page's og: metadata (site, title, description, thumbnail), fetched when the note scrolls into view, capped and parsed defensively, with the thumbnail riding the ordinary image cache; strict Tor keeps previews off entirely. Links are cleaned up too: the well-known tracking parameters (fbclid, gclid, the utm_* family) are stripped before display, before click-through, and before any preview fetch, so clicks don't carry their tags.

Clicking the new-notes chip is fast: the notes the live feed already saved paint immediately while the chip reads "Loading new notes…", and in multicolumn view the chip appears on the notes timeline only. Page landings no longer wait on a metadata round trip, the trust-graph's list fetch fires once per launch, and preview cards appear for extension-less web pages (a wiki slug, an App Store link used to render as a broken picture tile that suppressed its own card). The disappearing-image class closed its remaining roots: preview thumbnails, notifications-column images, and wire rows come back when memory pressure drops them.

The interoperability pass continues on two fronts: what a note can ask for, and where a publish goes. Zaps learned arithmetic: NIP-57 splits pay every receiver with relative weights, a receiver with no lightning pointer fails alone instead of failing the split, and NIP-75 goals render as cards with live progress and a raised-of target line. Comments on articles, pictures, videos and wikis whisper "on {name}'s note" in the notifications pane and open the parent by its coordinate (NIP-22). The feed grew surfaces for the kinds it already carried: content warnings veil until revealed (NIP-36), emoji shortcodes render their images (NIP-30), subject lines headline the row (NIP-14/24), and an unknown kind with an alt tag describes itself (NIP-31).

Publishing learned phase 2 of the NIP-65 routing: the app keeps per-event seen-on memory, deletion checks ask the relays where the original lived, profiles and relay lists publish to every known relay, personal kinds never broadcast, and a foreign inbox relay visits for one publish and leaves instead of joining the pool. Composing got friendlier: the emoji picker inserts the unicode character, the reaction heart grew a right-click quick-set, and emoji render in color at last. The mention typeahead matches display name, handle, NIP-05 and pubkey hex for anyone you interact with, seeded from the disk cache so names resolve on the first keystroke after a restart.

The screen learned to work in columns: a rail toggle opens a TweetDeck-style workspace of up to six live stream columns (Home, Articles, Notifications, Search, hashtags, authors, relays), each scrolling on its own, reordered by dragging and resized from its edge, the layout persisting across restarts; drilling into a thread or profile still takes the whole width, and Esc hands the columns back exactly as you left them. Pictures and videos with a d tag show comment counts and open their thread by address (NIP-22); voice notes render with the author's waveform and play inline (NIP-A0) behind the same guarded door as video; code snippets render in a monospace card with tap-to-copy (NIP-C0); and a kind the app has never heard of renders as a quiet "unrendered kind N" line instead of vanishing.

Under the hood, the batch got three five-lens audits (performance / system usage / memory / security / duplication) and the findings landed: the feed's caches are capped so a long session cannot grow them, secrets are wiped from freed heap, the single-instance socket verifies the connecting peer's uid and fails closed, the auth-URL door only opens http and https links, a closed relay column's socket no longer leaks, relay URLs pass the same screening everywhere they are typed or dialed, a voice row's tap refuses non-https attacker URLs, the comment-count fetches batch instead of one subscription per picture, and the publish, streaming, media-guard and FIFO-trim shapes collapsed into shared kernels.

The attachment-interop fix, hours after 0.7.0: a note's attached image or video now puts its URL in the event content beside the imeta tag. NIP-92 lets a client ignore an imeta that matches no content URL, and the strict ones did: the attachment showed in Satori and nowhere else. Comments get the same treatment, and an author who pastes the URL themselves gets no duplicate. Picture and video posts were already self-contained by design.

The interoperability release. Comments render and compose on articles (the reader grew a comments section with a reply affordance), comment counts ride the feed bubble, and publishes now additionally target the parent author's and tagged users' inbox relays, so a reply reaches authors who share no relay with us. The notifications pane gained an accurate tally strip with a 24h/7d/30d timeframe that remembers its choice.

The wallet got paste-time protection: relays inside wallet and bunker URIs are screened before any socket opens, private-address relays ask first, and consents are revocable in the settings pane. Cleartext ws:// relays are refused outright.

Media discipline: every pane pins exactly what is on screen, images stop disappearing while a page idles, RAM stops ballooning on photo profiles, and big pictures load now. Inline video plays its sound: the flatpak carries the PulseAudio permission. The pre-release five-lens audit fixed its verified findings: the pin registry is owner-keyed with a per-owner byte cap, closed panes release their pins, the consent ledger is written atomically with 0600 permissions, and preferences sync defers to newer local edits.

The replies-and-repairs release. Replies became surfaces, not a page: the composer sheet opens from any action row, thread included (the full form with attachments, alt text, preview and schedule in a card over the current pane), and the zap sheet became a proper overlay with its own card. Notifications wear their glyph anatomy: a reaction leads with its emoji, and reposts and quotes join the pane. Follow and Mute sit grouped on the profile, and the undo toast tells the truth past its deadline.

Signing got its biggest reliability pass yet: the first sign after login works against strict signers, the first sign after a restart carries the pairing secret the URI issued, and signing out and back in no longer strands the app on the login doors.

Under the hood: net_guard is the one IP authority, and the pre-release audit fixed ten verified findings: no more per-frame signature verification on zap rows, no resident tasks behind closed panes, the upload client and video player respect the IP authority, signer responses log method names only (the log file is 0600), and the single-instance socket read is capped.

An iteration release with no theme: the composer grew a Video tab (a deliberate video post is its own NIP-71 event, instant or scheduled, videos only), thread notes now carry the full action row the timeline has (reactions, repost, quote, reply, delete, zap), and the gallery carousel's arrows and position dots page the gallery instead of opening the thread.

Under the hood: paste-time screening refuses wallet and bunker URIs whose relays point at private addresses, the publish path refuses expired events and records its own deletions as tombstones at the door, and dependencies are current (cargo audit reports zero vulnerabilities). A CI workflow now gates every pull request, with a cargo-deny pass beside the audit.

New in the final cut: a store vacuum (satori-desktop --vacuum rebuilds the LMDB store offline, recovering the space deletions left behind) and an Alpine package beside the deb, rpm and flatpak - the first musl build.

The media and long-form release: attachments publish right (a note with an image is a kind-1 note with imeta; replies keep their thread), the Photo tab returns as its own picture-post surface, a full article composer (title, summary, cover upload, topics, markdown body) with strikethrough, task lists and tables in the reader, and hardenened media fetching (DNS-rebinding-safe resolution, search only asks search-capable relays).

The composer grew a polish pass of its own: previews on every tab (the article flips to the reader-faithful view, the rest show the draft as its feed card), session drafts for every post type with a two-step escape (the first escape saves and stays), a real editor (word motion, word deletion, line-wise home and end, a body that scrolls), fields that wrap and grow instead of clipping, video attachments in notes, a live reading time on the article, the type selector as a segmented control, and one filled action bar where Publish is unmistakable. A tag bug that kept satori's own polls from rendering as ballots is fixed.

The trust release: web of trust (in your network / outside, always annotated, never hidden), a duplicate-content spam filter with receipts, an auditable notification tier, and the four-lens audit fixes.

The polish release: live feed engagement, the relay hint model, scheduled posts, a full visual pass, and the quick wins (keyboard nav, emoji typeahead, multi-image carousel, alt text, relay health pane).
The first release: the whole client, from the follows timeline to inline video and zaps.
